minutes.headline: Board ratified a police hire and clock winder, heard flat hill drainage options, and committed two ARPA requests.
minutes.summary: The Select Board ratified a full-time police officer and the town clock winder, and heard the DPW director and an engineer on the Flat Hill Road culvert and Village of Flat Hill drainage. The board then worked through ARPA funding requests, committing two and deferring the rest pending a broken-down list, waived first refusal on a Chapter 61B parcel, and filled liaison assignments. The town manager read a statement on staffing vacancies.

public_comment.topic: Criticized the town manager's recommendation of an interim principal assessor and called on the board to act.
Thanked the investigation team, asked for status updates on the tax investigation and urged putting assessor hiring on hold until a plan exists.
Defended the interim assessor appointment as necessary to keep the office running.
Village of Flat Hill trustee representative objected to the lack of notice and disputed that the development caused the water problem.
Described decades of flooding from Flat Hill drainage and offered documentation.
Warned the lake drawdown timing risks missing the December 2024 bridge completion deadline.
Supported Mr. Marchetti's maintain-first approach to the drainage.
Noted ARPA funds must be spent by a deadline so delaying allocations is risky.

Commit ARPA money for PAC equipment upgrades at the stated amount.

Waive the town's right of first refusal for parcel 4 of Leominster Road (Chapter 61B).

what_happened.line: The board committed two ARPA requests, one for PAC equipment upgrades and one for the food pantry, and put the remaining requests off for a list broken down by department and item.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a full-time police officer, and unanimously ratified a town clock winder through June 30, 2024.

The board heard the DPW director and an engineer on the Flat Hill Road culvert and Village of Flat Hill drainage; it referred the basin question and the chair is to seek a meeting with the village trustees.
The board unanimously waived the town's right of first refusal on a Chapter 61B parcel on Leominster Road.
Public comment criticized and defended the interim principal assessor appointment, and a member said tax bills may be delayed and the town may need to borrow.

why_it_matters: ARPA is one-time federal money with a spending deadline, so which requests get funded and when decides what the town can pay for without raising taxes.
The assessing problem touches the timing of tax bills; if bills are delayed and the town has to borrow, residents could see the effect in when and how they pay.
